prompt: kubernetes OwnerReference blockOwnerDeletion missing permission error response
answer:
`blockOwnerDeletion: true` requires permission on the owner resource.

- Kubernetes API documentation states that the user needs **`delete` permission on the owner**; otherwise the API returns **HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity**.
- If the cluster has the `OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement` admission controller enabled—such as OpenShift—the controller also needs **`update` permission on the owner’s `/finalizers` subresource**.

Example RBAC rule:

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["<owner-api-group>"]
  resources: ["<owner-resource>/finalizers"]
  verbs: ["update"]
```

For example:

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["kubernaut.ai"]
  resources: ["remediationrequests/finalizers"]
  verbs: ["update"]
```

The error typically appears as:

```text
cannot set blockOwnerDeletion if an ownerReference refers to a resource you can't set finalizers on
```

Grant the controller’s ServiceAccount the required `/finalizers` permission, and ensure it has `delete` permission on the owner resource. If you use `oc auth can-i`, check the subresource with:

```bash
oc auth can-i update <owner-resource> --subresource=finalizers
```

Sources: [Kubernetes OwnerReference](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/definitions/owner-reference-v1-meta/#OwnerReference), [Kubernaut issue](https://github.com/jordigilh/kubernaut/issues/349#1), [ExternalModel RBAC troubleshooting](https://opendatahub-io.github.io/models-as-a-service/v0.2.0/configuration-and-management/troubleshooting-external-model-rbac/).
